raw_response:
I will keep cotton as my main crop because I already know how to manage it, I have 25 years of experience, and my farm has well irrigation, so I can support it through dry spells. But I do not want to put all 72 mu into one crop. My family has only 2 people and some labor is tied up off-farm, so I will split a smaller part into sunflower to spread risk and reduce labor pressure a bit. For cotton, I will use improved seed, put in moderate-to-strong fertilizer, irrigate several times, and stay on top of insects because cotton can lose yield quickly if I relax. For sunflower, I will keep management simpler, use hybrid seed, use less fertilizer and fewer sprays than cotton, and rely on it as a steadier secondary crop. I will use rotary tillage for both because it is practical for me at the start of the season and gives me a workable seedbed without making field work too heavy.
